title: Top K Frequent Elements
description:
# Top K Frequent Elements

Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the `k` distinct values that appear most frequently in `nums`. You may return the values in **any order**.

The test data guarantees that the top `k` set is unique, so there is no frequency tie that could make two different answer sets valid.

## Example 1:

**Input:** nums = [1,1,1,2,2,3], k = 2
**Output:** [1,2]

## Example 2:

**Input:** nums = [1], k = 1
**Output:** [1]

## Constraints:

*   `1 <= nums.length <= 10^5`
*   `-10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4`
*   `k` is in the range `[1, the number of unique elements in the array]`.
*   It is **guaranteed** that the answer is **unique**.

solutions.name: Bucket Sort
solutions.description:
## Approach

First count the frequency of every value. Since no value can appear more than `n` times, create buckets where bucket `f` stores all values with frequency `f`. Scan buckets from high frequency to low frequency until `k` values have been collected.

## Key Insight

This avoids comparing all elements by frequency. The frequency range is bounded by the input length, so bucket positions give a direct ordering from most frequent to least frequent.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Min Heap
solutions.description:
## Approach

Count frequencies, then maintain a min heap ordered by frequency. Push each distinct value into the heap; when the heap grows beyond size `k`, remove the smallest-frequency candidate. The remaining heap entries are the top `k` values.

## Key Insight

The heap stores only the current best `k` candidates, so this is useful when there are many distinct values but `k` is small. It trades the bucket array's linear scan for O(log k) heap maintenance.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n log k)
- Space Complexity: O(n + k)

solutions.name: QuickSelect
solutions.description:
## Approach

Count frequencies and store the distinct values in an array. Use QuickSelect to partition the array so that the `k` highest-frequency values land on one side of the pivot, then return those values.

## Key Insight

QuickSelect teaches selection without fully sorting all distinct values. It has good average performance, but unlike bucket sort it has a worst case that can degrade if pivots are unlucky.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n) average, O(n^2) worst case
- Space Complexity: O(n)
